correctness.rationale: In the truncated path basis the commutator has exactly the tensor coordinates a_i⊗b_{i+1}-b_i⊗a_{i+1}. Tensor rigidity gives one scalar per nontrivial nonzero run, unrestricted h-dimensional choices at singleton-one positions and unforced zero positions, and zero choices at zero positions adjacent to a nonzero one. These disjoint linear constraints prove the exact centralizer dimensions. A rank-one/rank-two site decomposition proves the block-weight generating function. The independent verifier constructs and Gaussian-eliminates actual commutator systems and separately enumerates finite pairs in bounded cases.

originality.rationale: The core claim is the elementwise, support-refined radical-centralizer spectrum for every m and parallel-arrow multiplicity h, not merely aggregate commuting-pair polynomiality. Hennecart–Perry (2022) studies radical commuting-pair counts for projective quiver representations and explicitly solves cases with paths of length at most two, covering the present m=2 aggregate subcase; that known case is excluded from novelty. Their inspected results do not imply the full radical-centralizer spectrum for the truncated family with arbitrary m. Historical implicit-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: An implicit identical enumeration in earlier centralizer or commuting-variety literature may exist despite searches.
The general one-arrow subcase has classical binomial-edge-ideal interpretations and is not independently represented as a new theorem.

value.rationale: Commutant size distribution and commuting probability are canonical invariants of a finite noncommutative algebra. The theorem classifies each radical element by its support pattern and proves exact multiplicities over all finite fields, all chain lengths and all parallel-arrow multiplicities. It derives a useful rational recurrence and determines extremal centralizers for h≥2, a structural and reusable result rather than an arbitrary finite census.
